title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
abstract: arXiv:2611.09213v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. translated_title: 机动车保险理赔中财务成本与碳足迹的联合建模：一个用于循环再利用汽车零部件采纳的BINAR(1)决策框架
translated_abstract: 机动车保险理赔管理日益面临双重目标：在控制理赔成本的同时，减少与车辆维修决策相关的温室气体排放。本文提出了一个受BINAR(1)依赖结构启发的二元离散时间建模框架，将财务理赔与维修相关碳足迹的动态联系起来，允许时间持续性、跨维度依赖性以及两个维度之间的正/负相关性。利用外部来源的排放因子和替换零部件的成本信息，我们在两种维修路径下对理赔的碳足迹进行了操作化：新零部件与循环经济再利用零部件（PIEC）。随后，我们开展了再利用零部件接受率各异的情景分析，并量化了其对预期货币支出和二氧化碳当量排放的联合影响。结果表明，更高的PIEC接受率可以同时……
tldr: 本文提出一个基于BINAR(1)结构的二元离散时间模型，联合刻画机动车保险理赔的财务成本与维修碳足迹，情景分析表明提高循环再利用零部件（PIEC）的接受率有望同时降低理赔支出与二氧化碳当量排放。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a bivariate BINAR(1)-based discrete-time framework that jointly models financial costs and repair-related carbon footprints in motor insurance claims, with scenario analyses showing that higher acceptance of circular reused parts (PIEC) can simultaneously reduce monetary outlays and CO2-equivalent emissions.
